answer.rationale: Primary objective is minimizing total cost of ownership without increasing delivery risk. Finance has mandated an 18% spend cut, the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and we have one decision this cycle. memory_c2 documents the low-cost vendor's recent onboarding success (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) — that's the only directly relevant track record here, and it warrants verification before committing the primary supply line. memory_c3 is about second-sourcing a constrained component — worth checking because the assembly line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so any risk to continuity matters even though the primary move is vendor switch, not dual sourcing. The other memories (c1, c4, c6) are incumbent-renewal patterns that don't apply if we're switching; c5 (defer) conflicts with the 14-day expiry and the hard mandate. Net: verify c2 (does the low-cost vendor's record hold up under scrutiny?) and c3 (does dual-sourcing/buffer logic suggest we should hedge rather than fully switch given 94% utilization with no slack?). Intended action: switch_primary_vendor — the mandate and the quote alignment make it the clearest path to the cost objective, pending verification that the low-cost vendor's integration and invoicing record is solid and that no hidden continuity risk at 94% utilization argues for a partial-switch or hedged variant.
